source.text: ወእምድኅረ፡ ዝ፡ አርአየኒ፡ መላእክተ፡ መቅሠፍት፡ *እለ፡ ድልዋን፡ ከመ፡ *ይመጽኡ፡ ወይፈትሑ፡ ኵሎ፡ ኀይለ፡ ማይ፡ ዘመትሕተ፡ ምድር፡ ከመ፡ ይኩን፡ ለኵነኔ፡ ወለአስተርእዮ፡ ለኵሉ፡ እለ፡ ይነብሩ፡ [ወየኀድሩ፡] ዲበ፡ የብስ።

translation.text: After this he showed me the angels of punishment, ready to come and release all the power of the water beneath the earth, so that it may be for judgment and manifestation[a] to all who live [and dwell] on dry land.[b]

footnotes.text: The printed noun አስተርእዮ is an abstract noun: Dillmann, column 299, gives manifestation, appearance, and revelation. The source coordinates two nominal expressions, “for judgment and for manifestation”; it does not separately say what is revealed. “It” retains the singular ይኩን without deciding whether water or its power is the precise antecedent.

This unit crosses from printed page 118 to 119. Charles prints [ወየኀድሩ፡], rendered [and dwell], in brackets; his note 5 calls it a dittography, reports omission by u and b x, and says the other manuscripts support the text. The source asterisks before እለ and ይመጽኡ are retained as edition signs, not translated as words. No manuscript was independently inspected.

translation.text: The Lord of Spirits commanded the angels who were coming not to raise their hands and to keep watch, because these angels were over the power of the waters.[a]

footnotes.text: Charles prints one negative ኢ before ያንሥኡ, a raising/lifting form; the raised 7 is an apparatus reference, not another source letter. Note 7 reports omission by u; note 8 gives a variant without the same causative vocalization. Dillmann, columns 636–637, supports raising or lifting, including hands. The following ወ coordinates the positive instruction to keep watch; “but” is not supplied. The source says “hands” without an overt possessive suffix; “their” identifies the commanded angels idiomatically in English.
